Examined PulseChain addresses: established roles and bounded
leads
Research date: 29 September 2026. All reads are retrospective. State uses PulseChain chain 369, block
27,659,393, hash 0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275.
Address register
Seven public addresses were examined. Six return empty runtime bytecode at the endpoint; the seventh
is the previously identified copied Arbitrum rollup contract. Empty current code is an observation, not a
claim about an address's entire historical behavior or owner.
Examined address Established role or current evidence
0x98c89980d1eae247ada3636ae27648f78e66e121 Sender and recipient of the examined MIM escrow
withdrawal; trace and receipt verified
0xfdbee32bcf68bb0ced033200373384a619c71967 Queued Aave proposals 219, 214 and 218; executed 218,
producing an outbound Optimism governance message
0xc000000be68420c4be47ee7004d0c69dfe57fd34 Empty runtime code and nonzero account nonce; no
protocol-control role established by this pass
0x48fc8b22ae5319786a8e25ef49b1b49942000000 Explorer's sampled recent transactions target 
0x0c4576ca1c365868e162554af8e385dc3e7c66d9, whose
published proxy source is named OgvStakingProxy; actual
staking action and authority require implementation-
specific interpretation
0x6e3bf3c7bd91144d694621298cb8da370479a7bb Sampled recent transactions include token-approval
selectors; no administrator transfer or bridge-mint role
established by these calls
0xbad9dff1026e59ea4c39cc3398aa5eb6f6f229ac Queued Aave proposal 225; sampled later transactions
interact with Reserve asset-adapter contracts
0x5ef0d09d1e6204141b4d37530808ed19f60fba35 Copied Arbitrum rollup proxy; 265 returned post-fork node-
confirmation events in the bridge census
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 58

The first, second, sixth and seventh entries connect directly to already examined bridge/governance
evidence. The remaining addresses are useful leads, but this study does not promote their presence in a
list into proof of common control. Account nonces include inherited activity; they are not counts of post-
fork governance transactions.
Transactions with strong protocol evidence
The e121 MIM withdrawal transfers 152.747067838559905107 MIM from the standard gateway to e121.
Its historical trace uses token transfer, and its accepted source-message metadata predates the fork. The
bridge study (Appendix 5) records the full trace, exact addresses, dates and comparison with the distinct
ARB bridgeMint transaction.
The BAD9 proposal-225 queue and FdbEE proposal-218 execution are successful public actions. Queue
and execution entry points are publicly callable subject to proposal state and timelock rules. They do not
alone prove that the submitter owns the executor or authored the proposal. Proposal 218 emits a
message through copied Optimism contracts; receiving-chain execution is not established. See the Aave
study (Appendix 2).
Additional leads and interpretation limits
The bounded explorer sample requested the latest 30 ordinary transactions per address, restricted to
blocks 17,233,000–27,659,393. It is not a complete transaction, token-transfer or internal-call history. A
returned empty list is not a conclusion that an address was inactive. T welve selected transactions were
also checked against successful RPC receipts and matching block headers; source classifications below
refer to published explorer code, not an assumption that every proxy has retained the same
implementation throughout history.
The 48Fc… sample includes a call to the OGV staking proxy. This introduces a concrete Origin-associated
lead. It is not itself evidence of OUSD bridge minting or Origin governance ownership. The proxy's 
published source identifies the contract family; the implementation and specific action would need
separate historical reconciliation.
BAD9's sampled transactions at block 26,768,729 target three contracts whose published names are 
RTokenAsset, Asset and Asset: 0x6e3b6b31c910253fef7314b4247823bf18d174d9, 
0xd5cc2875bbc53afbcc41bf04e7ba37f2894cbfa1, and 0x2c312da96f98a5b7822270f69afd2d7ae8e748dc. An example receipt
anchors the lead. All three recorded inputs use selector 0xf8ac93e8, matching refresh() in their published
interfaces and a read-only signature hash check. Refreshing an asset adapter should not be described as
minting an RT oken without the corresponding issuance and collateral-transfer evidence.
The FdbEE… sample also includes calls to a published SmartYield contract at 
0x4b8d90d68f26def303dcb6cfc9b63a1aaec15840. These are additional protocol interactions, not evidence of an
Arbitrum source deployment. No claim of a completed stablecoin bridge cycle follows from their
coexistence with Aave transactions.
Evidence preservation
Read-only address code/nonce results and bounded explorer responses are in artifacts/parb-core-
addresses-20260929/address_reads.json. Published target sources and selected receipt/header confirmations
are preserved in that same ignored batch directory. These records complement the earlier frozen bridge
and Aave event batches. No public transaction or local state-changing simulation was submitted during
this review.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 59
